sn1.46:1.1: The nymphs (_accharā_, “aquatics”) were known from Vedic times as beautiful dancers and musicians often romantically entwined with the _gandhabba_.
sn1.46:1.2: As horrifying as nymphs are seductive, the flesh-eating _pisāca_ (Sanskrit _piśāca_) arises in troops under cover of night and slips through the air wreaking havoc.
sn1.46:1.3: Delusion contains both desire and aversion.
sn1.46:2.4: Not really sure what dhamma means here, but the idea of samyutta suggests something like this, see eg AN 3.112.
